notes:
POC objective: prove Dedicated can meet dispatch-critical latency SLOs while supporting sustained throughput for peak windows. Short-hand notes from calls and tests: 
- Primary workload: real-time dispatch assistant + search/rerank for candidate vehicles.
- Targets: sustained 350-400 rps for simple dispatch queries; median latency <120ms; p95 <150ms; p99 ideally <400-500ms for standard prompts. CTO: "can't accept >200ms tail latency for dispatch-critical path" (quote).
- Cost sensitivity: medium — willing to commit to reserved capacity if unit economics meet thresholds (SE asked for model/quantization recommendations).
- Deployment: VPC peering, customer-managed NAT, KMS integration required. Data residency: US-only.
- Security: need SOC2 Type II evidence, SSO via SAML, audit logs retained 13 months, and optional HSM for keys.
- SLA asks: 99.9% availability, documented latency SLOs per route, credits for missed SLOs. Legal requested specific latency credit language (see linked doc).
- Internal constraints: SRE requires immutable IP list for peering; procurement expects final AR range before Q3 budget sign-off.
- Early decision factors: model variant (quantized vs fp16) impact on p99; batching trade-offs for throughput vs latency; KV/prefix cache effectiveness on dispatch prompts.
- Representative prompt examples used in tests included short dispatch intent (25-75 tokens), medium context (300-800 tokens including vehicle history), and long context (1k-2k tokens for post-hoc summarization).
poc_plan: Phase 0 - Prep (week 1): exchange runbook, security artifacts, firewall IPs, agree on prompt corpus
Phase 1 - Baseline load tests (week 2): 6h runs at 50/100/200/350 rps on ded preview cluster; collect p50/p95/p99 and token costs
Phase 2 - Soak tests (week 3): 48h continuous at target sustained throughput (350-400 rps) with synthetic traffic + periodic peak bursts to 500 rps
Phase 3 - Variant tuning (week 4): iterate model variants (fp16, Q4_8b), enable KV cache, measure cold vs warm KV hit rates
Phase 4 - SLA verification (week 5): run production-like mixed workload, validate autoscaling behavior and routing fallbacks, capture traces for SLOs
Phase 5 - Handoff (week 6): handoff runbook to ops, finalize reserved GPU sizing and contract SLA language
performance_targets: Peak burst: 500 requests/sec for up to 10 minutes
Availability: 99.9% (monthly), with defined credits for SLO misses
test_results_summary: Initial baseline run (2026-03-10) on Dedicated preview cluster: sustained 24h run showed stable median latency ~120ms at 380 rps for short dispatch prompts. p95 ~160ms, p99 spikes observed up to 620ms correlated with long-context summary requests and occasional GC/compaction events. CPU/GPU utilization suggests a need for reserved 6-8 GPU capacity for headroom (NVIDIA A10G equivalent tested). Enabling KV prefix caching reduced median latency by ~18% on warm hits and reduced p99 for medium prompts by ~25%. Next run will validate quantized model variant (8-bit) and tighter autoscaling thresholds to reduce tail spikes. Legal and network prerequisites remain blockers before multi-day soak can run on customer VPC.
